course_description:
Coverage of various advanced topics in control systems engineering: (i) observers and state estimation, (ii) multivariable systems in the frequency domain, (iii) robust control, and (iv) model predictive control.

This course focuses on the principles and tools used for designing and analysing feedback systems. It is specifically designed for students who are interested in utilising feedback for control in mechanical, electrical, and electro-mechanical systems, although broader application domains are touched on to give a sense of the breadth of the discipline.

The primary emphasis of the course is on state-space control. It begins by introducing the process of modelling various systems, including mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, biological, social, and informational systems, using ordinary differential and difference equations. Several detailed examples are covered throughout the course to reinforce the concepts. The course then explores the dynamic behaviour of models, covering stability and more complex nonlinear behaviour. Linear systems are examined as a special case of nonlinear systems, and state-space control laws are discussed, including state feedback, output feedback, and estimators.

The concepts of reachability and observability are introduced, providing insights into the selection of actuators and sensors for both engineered and natural systems. Additionally, topics such as Kalman filtering and optimal control are covered. While these topics could be individual courses themselves, this course aims to present them in a concise manner that allows for practical application in engineering.

Throughout the course, students are encouraged to apply these concepts to control physical systems, fostering a hands-on approach to learning and applying the material.

course_aims: The primary objective of this course is to enhance your understanding of the methods and principles employed in modern control engineering. By exploring the various concepts within control theory, the course aims to broaden your appreciation for the wide-ranging applications of these ideas and provide you with a comprehensive perspective on the field. Additionally, you will acquire the necessary knowledge to effectively utilize different design methods and gain practical experience in implementing control systems. By the end of the course, you will be equipped with the skills to confidently apply control engineering techniques and make informed decisions regarding their implementation.

learning_outcomes.description: State space modelling & simulation - Construct, linearise, discretise and simulate state-space models of linear and nonlinear dynamic systems using MATLAB and Simulink to analyse behaviour, stability and modelling limitations practically.

Reachability & observability - Evaluate reachability and observability in linear state-space systems using rank tests and Gramians, interpreting modes and implications for feedback, observers and practical engineering design decisions.

State feedback design - Design state-feedback controllers for linear SISO and MIMO systems using pole placement, LQR and integral action, assessing stability, accuracy, robustness and implementation constraints in practical contexts

Observer design & output feedback - Design Luenberger observers and output-feedback controllers, applying separation principles, feedforward strategies and digital implementation to estimate states, reject disturbances and evaluate closed-loop performance in applications.

Optimal control (LQR) - Derive and apply continuous and discrete LQR methods, selecting weighting matrices to meet objectives, relating outcomes to pole placement, and evaluating uncertainty and implementation limitations.

Optimal estimation (Kalman filter) - Derive and implement continuous and discrete Kalman filters for linear Gaussian systems, interpreting noise covariances and evaluating estimation accuracy, sensitivity and modelling assumptions in practice.

LQG synthesis - Synthesise LQG regulators by combining LQR and Kalman filter designs using separation, implementing controllers and evaluating robustness, performance and practical constraints against alternative control designs.

Integrated design & evaluation - Apply state-space modelling, LQR feedback and LQG synthesis to open-ended control problems, comparing robustness, evaluating performance, justifying trade-offs and communicating professional findings for engineering decisions.

Collaborate in Engineering Teams - Collaborate effectively in engineering teams to solve control problems by defining roles, managing tasks, communicating professionally and resolving technical and interpersonal challenges constructively during projects.

assessment_details.task_description: The problem-based assignment series consists of a collection of concise assignments designed to help you grasp fundamental concepts. These concepts are subsequently put into practice through the Control Systems Implementation Projects. Problem Based Assignment 1 (LO 1) will require you to develop a Matlab/Simulink model of a system and conduct simulations to analyse the system's response to various inputs. Problem Based Assignment 2 (LO 1) will require you to utilise Matlab for generating and analysing a phase portrait of a given system. Additionally, you will be tasked with determining a Lyapunov function for the system and using it to perform a qualitative analysis of system stability. Problem Based Assignment 3 (LO 1, 2, 3) involves the following tasks: (i) Creating a Simulink model of a balance system. (ii) Computing a linearisation of the system and comparing it with numerical functions available in MATLAB. (iii) Designing a stabilising control law for the linearised systems using state feedback. (iv) Developing a simulation that applies the designed stabilising control law to demonstrate its local asymptotic stabilisation of the system. Problem Based Assignment 4 (LO 1, 2, 3, 4) aims to enhance your proficiency in utilising the MATLAB Control Systems Toolbox, specifically in constructing state observers and state feedback controllers using the toolbox's available methods. The assignment emphasizes the application of state feedback for system stabilisation and provides an opportunity to explore the balance between observer poles and feedback poles. To access the detailed instructions and assessment criteria for each assignment, please refer to the assignment description provided on Blackboard. This task has been designed to be challenging, authentic and complex. Whilst students may use AI and/or MT technologies, successful completion of assessment in this course will require students to critically engage in specific contexts and tasks for which artificial intelligence will provide only limited support and guidance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. To pass this assessment, students will be required to demonstrate detailed comprehension of their written submission independent of AI and MT tools. Your performance will be evaluated through a demonstration of your control system and a presentation on its overall performance. As part of the assessment, you must also include an individual personal reflection. You should also reflect on your experience of working with the group, including communication, collaboration, decision-making, task allocation, and any lessons you learned from the process.
